newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean worker defects to South Korea - Yonhap.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean worker defects to South Korea - Yonhap.

text.p: A North Korean worker smuggled himself into the South and has sought political asylum, Yonhap news agency quoted the Agency for South Korean National Security Planning as saying on Friday.
Agency officials were not available to comment.
Yonhap said Lee Jong-hyon, 28, arrived in the southwestern port city of Inchon on Thursday from an unidentified third country after fleeing the communist state.
The South Korean intelligence agency was seeking more details on Lee, who worked as a labourer in North Korea, Yonhap said.
Lee was said to have left behind his parents, wife and one-year-old daughter in the communist North.
He is the latest of about 30 North Koreans who have defected to South Korea this year.

Quoting a report by the Unification Ministry, Yonhap said a total of 616 North Koreans had defected to the South since 1949, and the number had increased sharply since the "Great Leader" Kim Il-sung died in July 1994.
